correctness.rationale: The layer-cake lemma gives an exact n-dimensional polytope membership test including the zero vertex. Reflection containment gives a necessary and sufficient vertex test. Coordinate and alternating-triple inequalities prove lower bounds s>=3/2 at n=3 and s>=2 for n>=4. Candidate centers satisfy all reflected vertices by complementary interval decomposition (n>=4), exact three-dimensional inequalities (n=3), and exhaustive eleven-vertex positive variation at the exceptional endpoint (n=4). Paired quadruples force equality-case classification for all n>=5. The verified package contains rational checker output for 1,167 finite cases; analytic proof covers the infinite family.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general result for poset order polytopes gives their own reflection asymmetry, but the positive interval-incidence body is not proved to be an order polytope and its all-dimensional facet family is different. Euclidean sphere and inradius statements, though broader in their respective metric subjects, do not imply the present affine-reflection center classification.

value.rationale: The complete affine reflection invariant and the exact center locus are natural extremal-geometric questions for a canonical connected-block lattice-polytope family. The sharp stable value two coupled to a unique exceptional four-dimensional center segment is a genuine equality-case structure, distinct from published facet/Ehrhart and Euclidean inradius results. It has a compact all-dimensional proof and is not an ad hoc isolated computational value.
